patents.title: Speedy Heat-Induced Vacuum Assisted Process to Synthesize Quantum Dots
patents.description: A patented, ultrafast vacuum-assisted thermal process for synthesizing graphene and carbon quantum dots (GQDs/CQDs) from sustainable carbon precursors. The technology enables scalable production of highly crystalline quantum dots (~3.2 nm average size) in under one minute through a simple, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly process. Its high yield, rapid synthesis, and industrial scalability make it ideal for applications in sensing, healthcare, energy, electronics, and advanced nanotechnology.

blogs.title: Sense-XT Innovations Celebrates the Grant of a Patent for Rapid Quantum Dot Synthesis
blogs.excerpt: Sense-XT Innovations announces the grant of a patent for an innovative vacuum-assisted synthesis process that enables the rapid preparation of carbon quantum dots.
content: Sense-XT Innovations is proud to announce the grant of a patent for an innovative vacuum-assisted synthesis process that enables the rapid preparation of carbon quantum dots and graphene quantum dots.
To mark this important milestone, a copy of the granted patent was formally presented to the Honourable Vice-Chancellor of Jadavpur University, Prof. Chiranjib Bhattacharjee.

The patented technology introduces a fast and efficient method for synthesizing quantum dots within a remarkably short processing time. The process has the potential to support scalable production of advanced quantum materials for applications in sensing, healthcare, electronics, energy, and emerging quantum technologies.

Jadavpur University has been recognized as the patentee, while Prof. Sourav Sarkar, research scholars Manas Thakur and Sk. Najes Riaz—founders of Sense-XT Innovations—and the other contributors have been acknowledged as inventors.
This achievement reflects the strong research and innovation ecosystem fostered by Jadavpur University and the continued support of the National Quantum Mission and Qmet Tech.

Sense-XT Innovations remains committed to translating advanced research in quantum materials, nanotechnology, and sensing into reliable and impactful technologies. We look forward to building on this achievement and contributing to India’s growing quantum technology and deep-tech ecosystem.

blogs.title: Can India Become a Quantum-Tech Superpower?
blogs.excerpt: India’s quantum technology ecosystem is entering a decisive phase, driven by ambitious startups, growing institutional support, and the National Quantum Mission.
content: India’s quantum technology ecosystem is entering a decisive phase, driven by ambitious startups, growing institutional support, and the National Quantum Mission.

For many quantum startups, the early challenge has not been scientific capability but market confidence. Investors often view quantum technologies as long-term opportunities with uncertain commercial timelines. This has made funding, validation, and credibility major barriers for emerging companies.

Sense-XT Innovations experienced a similar journey. Founded by Manas Thakur, Sk. Najes Riaz, and Dr. Sourav Sarkar, the company was built on the belief that advanced scientific research must be translated into scalable and accessible technologies.
As Manas Thakur explains, strong research alone is not sufficient. Researchers must also develop an entrepreneurial mindset to transform laboratory innovations into commercially viable solutions.

The startup initially faced difficulties in securing grants and convincing investors about the potential of its technology. Selection under the National Quantum Mission became an important turning point. The recognition provided institutional validation, strengthened the company’s credibility, and helped investors better understand the commercial possibilities of quantum innovation.
Since then, Sense-XT Innovations has received increased interest from investors and ecosystem stakeholders.

However, private investment in India’s quantum sector remains limited. Government-backed initiatives such as the National Quantum Mission will therefore play a crucial role in supporting early-stage companies, reducing investment risk, and helping quantum startups move from research to real-world impact.
India’s journey toward becoming a global quantum-tech leader will depend on strong collaboration among government, academia, startups, industry, and private investors.

blogs.title: Sense-XT Recognized Among Startups Supported Under the National Quantum Mission
blogs.excerpt: Sense-XT Innovations is proud to be among the nine newly supported startups contributing to India’s growing quantum ecosystem.
content: India’s National Quantum Mission continues to make rapid progress across quantum communication, computing, sensing, and materials. A major milestone under the mission has been the successful demonstration of a 1,000-km quantum communication network using indigenous technology, strengthening India’s capabilities in secure digital infrastructure, defence, finance, and critical communications.

In parallel, the Government of India has expanded startup support under the National Quantum Mission, increasing the number of supported ventures to 17. Sense-XT Innovations is proud to be among the nine newly supported startups contributing to India’s growing quantum ecosystem.

Our work focuses on developing advanced quantum biosensors for early and reliable disease detection. This recognition strengthens our commitment to translating quantum science, nanotechnology, and biosensing research into scalable healthcare solutions with real-world impact.

The inclusion of Sense-XT alongside other promising quantum startups reflects the government’s continued focus on indigenous innovation, deep-tech entrepreneurship, and the commercialisation of emerging technologies. Support from the Department of Science and Technology, the National Quantum Mission, and associated ecosystem partners is helping early-stage companies build credibility, accelerate research, and move closer to market-ready solutions.
We sincerely thank NASSCOM DeepTech for highlighting and mentioning Sense-XT Innovations as part of this important national development.

As India advances toward global leadership in quantum technologies, Sense-XT remains committed to contributing through innovation, collaboration, and the development of accessible quantum-enabled healthcare technologies.

blogs.title: Sense-XT Joins India’s Expanding National Quantum Mission Ecosystem
blogs.excerpt: Sense-XT Innovations is proud to be among the newly supported startups in India's expanding National Quantum Mission.
content: India has achieved a major milestone under the National Quantum Mission with the successful demonstration of a 1,000-km quantum communication network using indigenous technology developed by QNu Labs. Completed within less than two years, the achievement reflects rapid progress toward the mission’s target of establishing a 2,000-km quantum communication network.
Alongside this advancement, the Government of India has expanded support to nine additional quantum startups, increasing the total number of supported ventures to 17.

Sense-XT Innovations is proud to be among the newly supported startups, alongside OrVis Semi, QuBeats, Quantum AI Global, Bloq, GDQ Labs, Quantum Biosciences, Bumblebee Instruments, and QUTE Electronics.

This recognition strengthens our commitment to developing indigenous quantum sensing and biosensor technologies for accessible and reliable healthcare applications while contributing to India’s growing quantum innovation ecosystem.
Read the full announcement: https://lnkd.in/gYM7V3V6

blogs.title: AI-Enabled Graphene Sensor Research Featured in Aajkal
blogs.excerpt: Our research on an AI-enabled, graphene-based sensor for dengue virus detection was featured in the Bengali daily Aajkal.
content: Our research on an AI-enabled, graphene-based sensor for dengue virus detection was featured in the Bengali daily Aajkal on August 19, 2024.

The project aims to develop a rapid and reliable diagnostic platform by combining advanced graphene sensing technology with artificial intelligence. It is being implemented with support from INUP–IIT Bombay and in collaboration with industry expert Dr. Soumi Sukla.
This recognition highlights our continued efforts to translate interdisciplinary research into accessible healthcare technologies for early disease detection.
